elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Rendered 4(a): "Customer may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to Kubient" — an unconditional Customer election, i.e. a convenience right.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The retained/edited notice period for Customer is "ninety (90) days written notice"; no 30-day mechanic was proposed.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund language anywhere in the rendered text; to the contrary, "Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates".

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: "Kubient may do so only effective at the end of the then-current Term" — the effective date is expressly tied to term end, so Vendor cannot exit mid-term (that residual right is natural-term non-renewal, assessed under RENEWAL).

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: "Customer may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to Kubient" — 90 days sits at the top of the 60–90 day band; the Initial Term is one (1) year, so the carve-out is not a multi-year lock-in.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: The only payment mechanic retained is "Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period" — fees earned in the ordinary course during the 90-day notice period, not a separate early-termination fee or penalty; the capping condition therefore does not bite.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: "Kubient may do so only effective at the end of the then-current Term" expressly ties the effective date of Vendor's convenience termination to term end, which is what the rule requires of an otherwise mutual notice mechanic.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: The edit converted the mutual sentence into a Customer-only predicate ("upon ninety (90) days written notice to Kubient") and then attaches Vendor by the shorthand "Kubient may do so only effective at the end of the then-current Term". Read literally, "do so" imports a notice given "to Kubient", i.e. Vendor noticing itself; no operative sentence obliges Kubient to give Customer 90 days' written notice, and the only express constraint on Kubient is the effective date, not a notice period.

reasons: Fallback is incomplete on one element: after the split, the 90-day notice obligation runs only in Customer's favour ("written notice to Kubient"), and Kubient's obligation is carried solely by the pronoun "do so", whose antecedent names Kubient as the notice recipient. Repair by stating Vendor's right in full: "...; Kubient may terminate this Agreement for any reason upon ninety (90) days' prior written notice to Customer, such termination to be effective only at the end of the then-current Term."

The end-of-term confinement itself is correctly drafted — the effective date is expressly anchored to the end of the then-current Term, so the residual Vendor right is non-renewal rather than mid-term convenience termination, satisfying that fallback element and (incidentally) the preferred no-mid-term-Vendor-exit element.

Early-termination fee element is satisfied without change: "all fees generated during the termination period" is ordinary revenue earned while the Agreement continues through the notice period, not a penalty; consider clarifying that for a Kubient end-of-term termination the "termination period" means the 90-day notice period, so the retained fee sentence cannot be read to stretch beyond three months.

Preferred level is not pursued and remains unmet (90 days rather than 30, and no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees); the rationale's explanation that this is a revenue-share model with no prepaid fees is a reasonable justification for targeting the fallback.

Minimality holds: the edit touches only the mutual convenience sentence, retains the Initial Term lock, the breach/insolvency rights in 4(b) and the fee sentence verbatim, and adds no extras (no survival tail, refund mechanic, or procedure) beyond the selected checklist.

Intent is preserved: renewal mechanics, breach termination, and the fee allocation survive without contradiction; the only defect is the unspecified Vendor notice recipient/period identified above, which is an element gap rather than a collateral change.
